answer: Forked state challenge: each identity must submit a hash-chain witness at random checkpoints, consuming its private seed and prior witness. Because clones cannot diverge, reusing one clone across identities yields identical chains or a detectable fork. The wharf node flags any chain collision. To pass, an attacker must keep separate mutable witness state and compute every checkpoint per identity, paying a fresh umber seal for each reset. A pearl audit fee is charged per challenged clone, so each Sybil identity has independent state and audit cost.
